Commentary.Commentary: Right. England lift the one-day trophy but India will not be too disappointed. They have got some well-earned momentum ahead of the T20I series. The multi-format scoreline reads 6-4 in favour of England, so all is set for a potentially cracking end to this tour. The T20Is begin from Friday, 9th July, 2021, with the first match scheduled to be in Northampton. The action starts from 6.30 pm local (1730 GMT). Do join us then. In the meanwhile, you can catch a plethora of international action coming up - WI-SA, Zim-Ban, WI-Aus and what not! Enjoy to the fullest. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

England Women's captain, Heather Knight, is disappointed with the result but calls it a good game. Puts the defeat to lack of runs and believes that they could not get the singles going and the lack of a set batter at the end hurt them. Feels that they bowled well but lost their composure towards the end. Is happy to have been tested by the Indians in this game. On being asked as to how did the English lose the game, Knight feels that no set batter went on to score big and that is what cost them the game. On pace off being the key to this match, Knight says that with the ODI series dusted, they were looking at players who could roll their arms over. Looks back at certain individual performances in this ODI series, naming Kate Cross and further adds that the team learnt a lot as well.

Victorious Indian captain and also the PLAYER OF THE MATCH, MITHALI RAJ, says that she never focusses on strike rates or other comments and only looks at her game. Stresses that she just wanted to concentrate on her own game and stay till the end. Adds that she wanted to guide Sneh Rana towards the end so that she does not throw her wicket away. Calls her phenomenal, as an allrounder, reminding all about her display in the Test and predicts that Rana will become one of India's greatest in the future. On being asked about her reaction to becoming the leading run getter in Women's International cricket, Mithali just smiles and modestly says that she is just happy to be here.

SOPHIE ECCLESTONE HAS BEEN NAMED THE PLAYER OF THE ODI SERIES. Says that she is disappointed with the result but enjoyed her displays. Adds that it is nice to have the confidence of the captain. Praises her own skipper. Heather Knight and also Sarah Glenn, for their performances.

England Women did well to put the pressure on India but lack of wickets hurt them. With wickets in hand, a batting side can always cover up the required rate. The lines and lengths were decent from the hosts, but the visitors batted with calmness and confidence. Skipper Mithali once again showed how important she is to the side, with a fine 75 from 86 balls. Strike rate concerns, anyone? For England, Sophie Ecclestone was the pick of the bowlers, with 2 wickets. Please stay tuned for the presentation...

At the halfway point, one always felt that England were 20-30 runs short and in the end, it did turn out that way. India put on a decent batting performance, which was all about partnerships. 46 for the opening wicket between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana, 50 between Harmanpreet Kaur and Mithali Raj, 33 between Mithali Raj and Deepti Sharma and in the end, 50 between Mithali Raj and Sneh Rana. Two batters crossed 40 but crucially, neither threw her wicket away and concentrated on forging partnerships. Things got a bit too close in the middle overs but that final stand between Mithali and Rana turned the tables over.
Comprehensive win from India. The series is alive and kicking, with the scoreline reading 6-4 in favour of England. 3 more matches to go and this sets up the T20I series coming up very nicely!

BEATEN! A length delivery, outside off, Verma looks to cut it but misses. The ball bounces over her blade.
Good length ball, on off, Verma defends it out.
A length ball, on off, Verma pushes it to point.
Kate Cross comes into the attack now.
On off, worked to cover.
FOUR! This is Mandhana's fifth boundary. On a length, outside off, Mandhana stays back and waits for the ball. She cuts it behind point for a boundary. Amazing shot.
A ful length delivery, on off, Mandhana drives it to mid off.
On off, cut to point.
A length ball, on off, pushed to cover.
FOUR! This is classic Smriti Mandhana! A fuller length ball, outside off, Mandhana drives it through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! A boundary to end the over. A length ball, on middle Verma shuffles and lifts it down the ground. The ball goes over the mid on fielder for a boundary.
On a length, on off, Verma works it to point.
A bouncer on middle, Verma ducks under it.
On off, kept out by Verma.

Brilliant fielding in the deep by Sophia Dunkley. A full length ball, on off, Smriti Mandhana flicks it to deep square leg. Sophia Dunkley covers a lot of ground to her left and makes a diving stop. Just a run off it.
On a length, on off, Verma opens works it to third man again for another single.
Serves a length ball, on off, Verma guides it to third man for a single.
A length ball, around off, Verma chips it over the bowler's head to mid off. If the ball had stayed low Verma was a goner.
A full length ball, on off, Smriti Mandhana drives it to the left of mid off for a single.
A length ball, on off, close to the body, Smriti Mandhana cuts it to point.
On off, defended back to the bowler.
A length ball, on off, Verma works it to the leg side off the inner blade. Single taken.
EDGY FOUR! Third boundary in the over. A full length ball, on off, Smriti Mandhana looks to push it to cover. The ball takes the outside edge and goes through point and gully for a boundary.
A length ball, on off, Mandhana is solid in her defense. Smart batting.
FOUR! Absolutely Gorgeous! A full length ball, outside off, swinging away a little. Smriti Mandhana leans in and creams it through the cover region for a boundary.
Full and outside off, Mandhana drives it to cover.
FOUR! Nicely picked up. A length ball, on off, Mandhana pulls it through the square leg region for a boundary.
An outswinger. Full and outside off, Verma pushes it to cover and gets a single.
Full, around middle, driven straight to mid on once more.

Similar ball, this time Mandhana flicks it to the other side of mid on, her left, but it is cut off. Not taking any risks at this point of time, is Mandhana. No need to, with Shafali in the middle. India Women need another 208 from 259 balls.
Very full, on middle, Smriti Mandhana drives it beautifully but finds mid on.
Another wide, down the leg side again, SM misses her flick once more.
WIDE. Full, down the leg side, Smriti misses her flick. India Women need another 209 from 261 balls.
Outside off, Shafali Verma chops it down to third man for a run. The stand moves to 10 from 21 balls.
Landed around off, angling away, Mandhana goes back, allows the ball to come to her and guides it behind point for a single.
Fuller, around middle, now Smriti Mandhana walks into the shot and pushes this towards mid on.
On a good length, around off, solid in defense is Verma.
Full, around off, Shafali is well outside her crease as she blocks this towards cover.
Fuller, around middle, moving away, Shafali Verma gets across and defends it to the leg side.
On middle and leg, shaping back down, Smriti tucks this through square leg for a single.
Around off, shaping back in, Mandhana defends it with the full face of the bat towards mid on.
Full, around off, swinging in, Smriti Mandhana drives it towards mid off.
FOUR! Shafali Verma hands India their first boundary of the run chase. Full, outside off, Shafali comes forward and carves it over cover.
That's nicely played. Full, around middle, Mandhana reaches out, gets to the pitch of the ball, pushes it towards mid off and takes a good single.
Around leg, angling away, Smriti Mandhana defends it towards mid on.
In the air... safe again! Outside off, fuller in length, Shafali walks down the track and has a mighty swing. Skews it over Sophie Ecclestone at point running back. A single taken.
Outside off, swinging in again, Shafali Verma walks into the shot and drives it towards mid on.
Full, outside off, swinging in, watchfully defended.
Anya Shrubsole to bowl with the second new ball.

In the air... safe! Full and wide outside off, Verma walks down the track and looks to drive, slicing it behind point for a single. An excellent opening over. India Women need 219 more to win from 276 balls.
Outside off, pushed straight to point again.
Walks into this shot, does Shafali and pushes away from her body again, towards point.
Beaten. Absolute beauty. On a length, outside off, Shafali Verma plays away from her body and pushes at it. The ball pitches and then moves away, beating the outside edge.
On a good length, around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, on a length, played straight to cover.
